title: Data Visualization
text: Working primarily in R and RStudio, I have worked extensively with the tidyverse, ggplot2, Shiny, pkgdown, and various bespoke R packages. My GitHub is the best resource for assessing my competencies in data visualization and analyses, but I’ve included a few projects during my time at GMRI that best represent my work.

title: Data Visualization
text:
Adaptation Hub
For the Understanding Fisheries Climate Impacts section of the Climate Adaptation Resource Hub for Fishing Communities, I generated reports highlighting historical fisheries trends and future biomass projects for 16 fishing communities in the Northeast US. Those reports were then embedded into a leaflet map, which can be accessed below.

title: Data Visualization
text:
Species Shifts
During my time at GMRI, I worked extensively with a number of federal fishery dependent and independent data sets for a variety of projects. One such project, with the Mid-Atlantic Fisheries Management Council, leveraged many of these data sets to understand shifts across management jurisdictions. As such, and given my intimate knowledge of these data sets, I built an R package to compile all data cleaning and plotting functions into one central location. This would also avoid any duplicative efforts on behalf of my coworkers. The package is available to the public but its functionality is contingent on access to these federal data sets.
For examples of my most common data visualizations, please navigate to About and select Visualizing federal fisheries data.

title: Science Communication & Engagement
text: I began my science communication career as a volunteer exhibit guide at the South Carolina Aquarium in Charleston, South Carolina. Over the years, I’ve held multiple public engagement roles within the natural sciences, and made multiple contributions to science and sustainability publications. Storytelling is at the core of scientific research, as we try to understand and find meaning in the world around us.

title: Climate & Fisheries Research
text: I am primarily interested in the localization and contextualization of large scale climate and ecosystem change. Given the complexities of fisheries and how they are influenced by not only environmental change but regulatory, market, and behavioral trends as well, working in fisheries has been an excellent ecosystem for applying climate decision frameworks. In quantifying changes in commercial fishing, I hope to aid people and institutions as we understand, navigate, and manage the impact climate change has on our daily lives.

title: Carly S. Lovas
text: Hi, and welcome to my portfolio. I am a quantitative marine ecologist, focusing on the impacts of climate-driven ocean warming on fisheries socio-ecological systems. I work primarily with federal fisheries independent and dependent survey data, including (but not limited to) NOAA Northeast Fisheries Science Center Spring-Fall Bottom Trawl Survey, NOAA Fisheries Marine Recreational Information Program, Greater Atlantic Regional Fisheries Office Commercial Harvest Permits and Fisheries Observer Data. I have supported multiple projects funded by NOAA and Maine Sea Grant, the National Science Foundation BioOce Program, and Mid-Atlantic Fisheries Management Council via the Inflation Reduction Act. All of these projects sought to quantify shifts in distribution of commercially viable marine species, and the understand the potential implications on marine fisheries in the Northeast United States. As a researcher, I am motivated to quantify climate-driven shifts in marine species distribution, and develop frameworks to support more dynamic, adaptive, and climate-resilient commercial fisheries. I am passionate about leveraging lived experience and knowledge with scientific information to building well-informed, engaged, and resilient communities. Please take this opportunity to peruse my work, and please don’t hesitate to reach out for any inquiries or opportunities.
